activities.title: Language Development: Community Circle Time
activities.content:
Greetings
• Welcome pupils and have them sit in a circle. 
• Follow the normal greeting routine.
• Have the pupil that was just greeted, turn to the pupil on their right and greet 
them. This continues all the way around the circle.
Theme Discussion
• Before school starts, bring in two items related to the theme to show the pupils. 
Put the items in the center of the circle. If no items are available, draw two 
pictures on the board instead.
• Say: Toêêere men en ndee yontere ko fii (kulle). Piiji ngonɗi ɗi he hakkunde he, na 
heɓani en nafoore e toêêere hee.
• Hold up one of the items from the center of the circle. 
• Say: Ɗum ko hoɗum?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer.
• Say: Ko hoɗum mbaawɗaa kam haalan fii ɗum?
• Call 2-3 pupils at random to answer. Repeat with the second item.
• Say: Ɗii piiji ko hoɗum ɗi wonani en?

• Give pupils one minute to think. You may suggest they close their eyes to picture 
their response. Then choose one of the following options for discussion: call on 
3 pupils at random, Turn and Talk (have pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go 
around the circle and allow every pupil to answer (only if the answer is short), or 
have pupils take turns acting out answers.
• Encourage pupils to bring in their own items relating to the theme throughout the 
week.

activities.title: Letter of the Week
activities.content:
Learning Letter: "a"  "A" 
• Write the small letter "a" very big on the board. Point to the letter.
• Say: Ndee yontere ko ngal alkulal jangeten. Ngal alkulal waɗat hito /a/. Haalden 

hito ngo /a/.

times slowly.

• Say: Alkulal gootal woni ɗo e ko hito /A /. Eɗen nji'a ɗum e fuɗɗorde konngol, innde

activities.title: Writing
activities.content:
Learning Names
• Say: En janngat no inɗe men ɗe  winndirtee. En purtat juuɗe ndilinenɗe haade en 
fuɗɗo.
• Warm up exercise: have pupils push their palms together as hard as they can for 
10 seconds. Then release and shake hands for 10 seconds. Repeat two more times.
• Give each pupil their individual name card.
• Have pupils go through the following steps: 
• Pupils trace the letters on the name card with their fingers.
• Pupils trace the letters of their name on their desks or on the ground. 
• Pupils write their name on paper. 
• Monitor pupils through each step to make sure they are forming the letters correctly. 
Provide guidance as needed either verbally or by writing the letter(s) for the pupil 
to trace.

•  Say: En janngat kelme kese fii mbaawen faam taali ko feewi. Taalol ngol na wa ɗi 
kelme mbaɗɗe nafoore ɗe poɗɗen janngu.

activities.title: Before Reading & Reason to Read
activities.content:
Comprehension: Visualization 
• Say: Miijoɗen ko taalol ngol woni.
• Read the title of the story but do NOT show the illustration.
• Say: He ndeer miijomon he, mbaɗee natal he ko cikkuɗon taalol ngol haalata. Ko 
njiiɗon?
• Give the pupils a minute to make the picture in their mind. 

• Turn and Talk: Have pupils turn to the pupil next to them to talk about what they 
are visualizing in their minds. After two minutes, gather pupils back as a group. 
Choose a good example you heard from a pupil and share it with the class.
• Say: Jooni, fonndindiren nate mon ɗe e nate taalol ngol ji'en honoɗe mbaadi.
• Show the picture for the story.
• Say: Hoɗum njiiɗon he natal he ko nanndi e natal ngal njiiɗon ngal e miijoojimon 
hee?
• Give the pupils a minute to think about what was the same. Then call on a pupil at 
random asking for what they see. Make sure the pupil's description relates to the 
picture and the story.
• Learn New Print Concepts
• Say: Si ɗen jannga, janngen kelme ɗee wootere wootere. Taalol na waɗi kelme 
keewɗe, ɗe jangeten e ɗerol kala.
• Hold up the book. Read the title slowly and point to each word.
• Call on a pupil at random to come and point to each word of the title as you read.

activities.title: Comprehension: After Reading
activities.content:
Factual Question: Review All  
• Read the title of the story. Call on a pupil at random to answer each of the following 
factual questions:
Question 1: Ko hoɗum Bacci laarat no? (Jaabawol: Ndiyam)
Question 2: Ko hoɗo Bacci tawi ndiyam ɗam? (Jaabawol: He ndeer Siwo)
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Help pupils 
find the part of the story that contains the answer.Inferential Questions: Main Idea
• Say: Taalol kala na heɓi hoore haala ko ngol firata. Faandaare nde woni ko taalol

story is mostly about.

activities.content:
Learning Names
• Say: Ɗen ngara janngu no winndirtee inɗe menɗe. haade en fuɗɗo en portat 
juuɗe dilinen ɗe.
• Warm up exercise: have pupils push their palms together as hard as they can for 
10 seconds. Then release and shake hands for 10 seconds. Repeat two more times.
• Give each pupil their individual name card.
• Have pupils go through the following steps: 
• Pupils trace the letters on the name card with their fingers.

• Pupils trace the letters of their name on their desks or on the ground.
• Pupils write their name on paper. 
• Monitor pupils through each step to make sure they are forming the letters 
correctly. Provide guidance as needed either verbally or by writing the letter(s) 
for the pupil to trace.

pupils are having difficulty, give an example and ask if that it is true for them too. 
Example: Once I saw butterflies on a plant. 
• NOTE: Be sure to ask different pupils throughout the week. If a pupil is struggling, 
ask them prompting questions, such as: Have you ever [insert event from story]? 
Monitor and keep track of how well the pupils are able to make connections that 
make sense and relate to the story.

activities.title: Comprehension: After Reading
activities.content:
Making Connections
• Read the title of the story again and show the illustration.
• Say: Ko hoɗum taalol ngol janngini on he nguurndam mon? Mumne ɗee miijoɗon

connection with the story. Walk around and listen to what pupils are saying.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the following letters on the board: (a, b, c, d, e ɗ ,f)
• The letters should be large enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly 
spaced out in a line that is eye level for the pupils. After writing each letter:

• Say: Ɗum ko alkulal hongal? Ko hito hongo ngal waɗata?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let them 
know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that 
have been learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say: Mi waɗat hito, siɗa tami kartal jogingal alkulal ngal, aan e wajiraawo maa ɗon 
poti taɗɗu to alluwal to takkon kartal ngal e dow alkulal he.
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are 
having difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.
• NOTE: Keep track of which pupils are having difficulty recognizing specific letters. 
Also see if there is a specific letter most of the class is struggling with. If this 
happens, stop and review the letter before continuing with the game.

activities.content:
Reviewing Names
•  Say: E åen ngara rewto hono innɗe winndirtee. Haade en fuɗɗo, porten juuɗe 
men.
• Warm up exercise: have pupils tap their fingers one at a time on their thumb 
(start with pointer, then middle, then ring, then pinky). Do one hand at a time. As 
pupils learn the movement, try doing both hands at the same time.
• Give each pupil their individual name card. 
• NOTE: Have pupils write their name on their paper. If pupils cannot complete 
their name, try to find a way to help them. For example, write the letters and have 
them trace. Another option: see if pupils can write their name without looking at 
their name card.

activities.title: Alphabet
activities.content:
Name Card
• Put all the pupils' name cards on the floor or table. 
• Say: Mi noddat on ngaron yeeso fii ndaaron innåe mon. Si on yi'i innåe mon åe 
okkon kam kartal ngal.l
• Have pupils come up 2-3 at a time. When they bring you their card, point to their 
name and as they say it move your finger along the letters. Then have the pupil 
clap the syllables in their name.

• NOTE: Monitor which pupils are able to identify their name and clap the syllables, 
and those pupils who have difficulty. If pupils don't recognize their name, try to 
find a way to help them remember it. For example, write it in large print on their 
notebook or a piece of spare paper. Ask them to take it home and trace the letters 
with their finger a few times. If pupils have difficulty clapping the syllables in their 
name, clap with them as you slowly say their name.
